raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

<!-- PR title: [Type] scope: title, or [Type] [Hardware] scope: title.
Type: Feat, Fix, Refactor, Perf, Doc, Test, CI, or Chore.
Scope: any module or model name (no fixed list or letter-case restriction), e.g. attention, qwen3, or flash-attn.
Hardware: optional single tag without spaces. Use uppercase hardware tags (AMD, NVIDIA, NPU, MI300X), except for exactly these four spellings: Intel, Apple, Huawei, Ascend.
Title: no letter-case restriction.
Reverts: use GitHub's default title, Revert "original title".
Examples: [Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing; [Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

Currently, only CUDA GPUs have a device-level mm feature transport (cuda_ipc/cuda_vmm); NPU falls back to CPU transport with extra host↔device copies. This PR adds npu_ipc, an NPU equivalent of cuda_ipc that shares multimodal features zero-copy through a bounded NPU IPC memory pool.

## Modifications

- Added `npu_ipc` as a new `--mm-feature-transport` option, providing CUDA IPC-equivalent zero-copy multimodal feature transport on Ascend NPUs, with the same bounded memory pool and CPU fallback behavior.
- Added validation for npu_ipc: requires the NPU platform and a single node.
- Generalized the transport core to be device-agnostic: stream-ordered value operations now dispatch to CANN's `acl.rt.value_write`/`value_wait` on NPU (64-bit, 8-byte-aligned control words) and to CUDA driver ops on GPU; IPC handles use `_share_npu_`/`_new_shared_npu` on NPU.
- Reused the existing IPC pool path in `BaseMultimodalProcessor` for `npu_ipc`.
- Reserved `SGLANG_MM_FEATURE_CACHE_MB` from the KV cache budget for `npu_ipc` pools.
- Replaced hard-coded `torch.cuda` calls and `device.type == "cuda"` checks with device-agnostic equivalents in the feature-consuming paths (`mm_utils`, `schedule_batch`, `kimi_k25`, `kimi_k3`, `qwen3_vl`).
- Added unit tests for server-args parsing, transport config selection, and real-device NPU IPC transport across processes and devices.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

```
Qwen3.6-35B-A3B

sgl-eval run mmmu_pro_vision \
--base-url http://127.0.0.1:8234/v1 \
--temperature 0 \
--max-tokens 81920 \
--num-threads 32 \
--num-examples 128

## baseline

== mmmu_pro_vision ==
128 examples (single-shot)  |  1765.0s  |  1150 tok/s  |  2.0M tokens

* score                =  75.78%
  stop_rate            =  87.50%
  truncated_rate       =  12.50%  [warn: hitting max_tokens]
  error_rate           =  0.00%
  avg_input_tokens     =  1,176.6 tokens
  avg_output_tokens    =  15,856.3 tokens
  avg_thinking_tokens  =  15,418.4 tokens

## with npu_ipc

== mmmu_pro_vision ==
128 examples (single-shot)  |  1779.2s  |  1091 tok/s  |  1.9M tokens

* score                =  76.56%
  stop_rate            =  88.28%
  truncated_rate       =  11.72%  [warn: hitting max_tokens]
  error_rate           =  0.00%
  avg_input_tokens     =  1,176.6 tokens
  avg_output_tokens    =  15,157.7 tokens
  avg_thinking_tokens  =  14,737.8 tokens
```

After enabling npu_ipc, no accuracy degradation was observed within the fluctuation range.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->

*bench scripts*

```
sglang serve --model-path /home/weights/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B \
--trust-remote-code \
--mem-fraction-static 0.8 \
--attention-backend ascend \
--tp-size 2 \
--mm-attention-backend ascend_attn \
--enable-multimodal \
--mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 \
--host 127.0.0.1 \
--port 8234 \
--mm-feature-transport npu_ipc

python -m sglang.bench_serving \
--dataset-name image \
--backend sglang-oai-chat \
--host 127.0.0.1 \
--port 8234 \
--max-concurrency 1 \
--num-prompts 1 \
--warmup-requests 1 \
--random-input-len 30 \
--random-output-len 1024 \
--random-range-ratio 1 \
--image-resolution 1024x1024 \
--image-count 64 \
--seed 1 \
--request-rate inf

python -m sglang.bench_serving \
--dataset-name image \
--backend sglang-oai-chat \
--host 127.0.0.1 \
--port 8234 \
--max-concurrency 16 \
--num-prompts 32 \
--warmup-requests 16 \
--random-input-len 30 \
--random-output-len 1024 \
--random-range-ratio 1 \
--image-resolution 1024x1024 \
--image-count 7 \
--seed 1 \
--request-rate inf
```

*bench result*

```
# concurrency=1，images=64/req

## Baseline

----------------End-to-End Latency----------------
Mean E2E Latency (ms):                   17058.64  
P99 E2E Latency (ms):                    17058.64  
---------------Time to First Token----------------
Mean TTFT (ms):                          4224.43   
P99 TTFT (ms):                           4224.43
-----Time per Output Token (excl. 1st token)------
Mean TPOT (ms):                          12.55    
P99 TPOT (ms):                           12.55   

## mm_feature_transport=npu_ipc

export SGLANG_MM_FEATURE_CACHE_MB=2048  # 64 images require about 1.5 GB of memory

----------------End-to-End Latency----------------
Mean E2E Latency (ms):                   15301.17   
P99 E2E Latency (ms):                    15301.17  
---------------Time to First Token----------------
Mean TTFT (ms):                          2683.41    
P99 TTFT (ms):                           2683.41  
-----Time per Output Token (excl. 1st token)------
Mean TPOT (ms):                          12.33   
P99 TPOT (ms):                           12.33  


# concurrency=16，images=7/req

## Baseline

----------------End-to-End Latency----------------
Mean E2E Latency (ms):                   37194.55  
P99 E2E Latency (ms):                    37586.65  
---------------Time to First Token----------------
Mean TTFT (ms):                          9344.76   
P99 TTFT (ms):                           13994.51
-----Time per Output Token (excl. 1st token)------
Mean TPOT (ms):                          27.22     
P99 TPOT (ms):                           34.16

## mm_feature_transport=npu_ipc

----------------End-to-End Latency----------------
Mean E2E Latency (ms):                   34419.52  
P99 E2E Latency (ms):                    34869.12  
---------------Time to First Token----------------
Mean TTFT (ms):                          6986.50   
P99 TTFT (ms):                           11407.64 
-----Time per Output Token (excl. 1st token)------
Mean TPOT (ms):                          26.82     
P99 TPOT (ms):                           32.62
```

| Scenario | Metric | cpu (baseline) | npu_ipc | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| concurrency=1, 64 images | TTFT | 4224 ms | 2683 ms | -36.5% |
| | E2E latency | 17059 ms | 15301 ms | -10.3% |
| | TPOT | 12.55 ms | 12.33 ms | ~0 |
| concurrency=16, 7 images/req | TTFT (mean) | 9345 ms | 6987 ms | -25.2% |
| | E2E latency (mean) | 37195 ms | 34420 ms | -7.5% |
| | TPOT (mean) | 27.22 ms | 26.82 ms | ~0 |

TTFT drops 25-37% because multimodal features no longer round-trip through
CPU memory between processes; the gain scales with the number of images.
TPOT is unchanged, confirming the transport only affects prefill. End-to-end
improvement is diluted by the long decode phase (1024 output tokens).

## Checklist

- [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

+"""Real-device coverage for the npu_ipc multimodal feature transport.
+
+Verifies the two NPU-specific assumptions behind the shared stream-ordered
+pool (``sglang/srt.multimodal.transport.memory_pool``):
+aclrtValueWait/aclrtValueWrite work on the consumer's IPC-opened mapping —
+so the ready/ack words need no interprocess event — including when the
+consumer sits on a different NPU than the pool.
+
+Each test spawns a producer that wraps a feature into the bounded pool and a
+consumer process that opens it, waits the ready word, reads the slice, and
+acknowledges the lease.
+"""
+
+import gc
+import multiprocessing as mp
+import queue
+import time
+import unittest
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.multimodal.transport.cuda_ipc import MmItemMemoryPool
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_npu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+# Registered on a two-NPU suite so the cross-device case actually runs.
+register_npu_ci(est_time=30, suite="base-b-test-2-npu-a3")
+
+POOL_BYTES = 1 << 20
+# One consumer slot keeps the acknowledgement independent of the parallel
+# state, which a bare spawned process has not initialized.
+CONSUMER_SLOTS = 1
+
+
+def _produce_pooled_tensor(proxy_queue, consumer_done, result_queue):
+    """Create a tokenizer-worker-like NPU IPC pool in a spawned producer."""
+    pool = source = proxy = None
+    try:
+        torch.npu.set_device(0)
+        pool = MmItemMemoryPool(
+            memory_size=POOL_BYTES,
+            recycle_interval=0.01,
+            base_gpu_id=0,
+            consumer_count=CONSUMER_SLOTS,
+        )
+        source = torch.arange(35, dtype=torch.float32, device="npu").reshape(5, 7)
+        expected = torch.arange(35, dtype=torch.float32).reshape(5, 7).tolist()
+        proxy = pool.wrap_tensor(source, use_pool_handle_cache=True)
+        if proxy is None:
+            raise RuntimeError("test tensor did not fit in the NPU IPC pool")
+        proxy_queue.put((proxy, expected))
+        if not consumer_done.wait(timeout=60):
+            raise TimeoutError("consumer did not acknowledge the NPU IPC tensor")
+        deadline = time.monotonic() + 30
+        while time.monotonic() < deadline:
+            if pool.active_lease_count == 0:
+                break
+            time.sleep(0.05)
+        else:
+            raise TimeoutError("pool did not observe the consumer acknowledgement")
+    except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover - returned to the parent
+        result_queue.put(("error", repr(exc)))
+        return
+    finally:
+        del proxy, source
+        if pool is not None:
+            pool.shutdown()
+            del pool
+        gc.collect()
+    result_queue.put(("ok", None))
+
+
+def _consume_pooled_tensor(proxy_queue, result_queue, rebuild_device=0):
+    """Open the pool and read the slice in a spawned scheduler-like consumer."""
+    try:
+        torch.npu.set_device(rebuild_device)
+        try:
+            proxy, expected = proxy_queue.get(timeout=60)
+        except queue.Empty:
+            raise TimeoutError("consumer never received the NPU IPC proxy")
+        # This reconstruct value_waits the ready word the producer wrote in
+        # another process, on a mapping opened from the producer's handle.
+        reconstructed = proxy.reconstruct_on_target_device(rebuild_device)
+        torch.npu.synchronize()
+        if reconstructed.cpu().tolist() != expected:
+            raise AssertionError("the consumer read back the wrong feature")
+    except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover - returned to the parent
+        result_queue.put(("error", repr(exc)))
+        return
+    # The process-wide pool mapping dies with this process; the transport
+    # has no manual cache teardown because the cache lives exactly as long
+    # as the process holding it.
+    result_queue.put(("ok", None))
+
+
+def _run_producer_consumer_test(test, consumer_device=0):
+    ctx = mp.get_context("spawn")
+    proxy_queue = ctx.Queue()
+    producer_results = ctx.Queue()
+    consumer_results = ctx.Queue()
+    consumer_done = ctx.Event()
+    producer = ctx.Process(
+        target=_produce_pooled_tensor,
+        args=(proxy_queue, consumer_done, producer_results),
+    )
+    consumer = ctx.Process(
+        target=_consume_pooled_tensor,
+        args=(proxy_queue, consumer_results, consumer_device),
+    )
+    producer.start()
+    consumer.start()
+    try:
+        try:
+            consumer_result = consumer_results.get(timeout=120)
+        except queue.Empty:
+            test.fail("NPU IPC consumer did not report in time")
+        consumer.join(timeout=10)
+        if consumer_result[0] != "ok":
+            test.fail(f"NPU IPC consumer failed: {consumer_result[1]}")
+        test.assertEqual(consumer.exitcode, 0)
+
+        # The consumer's process-wide pool mapping died with its process,
+        # so the producer may now destroy the shared allocation.
+        consumer_done.set()
+        try:
+            producer_result = producer_results.get(timeout=120)
+        except queue.Empty:
+            test.fail("NPU IPC producer did not finish after the consumer exited")
+        test.assertEqual(producer_result[0], "ok", producer_result[1])
+        producer.join(timeout=10)
+        test.assertEqual(producer.exitcode, 0)
+    finally:
+        # Whatever failed, never strand the producer on its wait for the
+        # consumer, and leave no child process behind.
+        consumer_done.set()
+        for process in (consumer, producer):
+            if process.is_alive():
+                process.terminate()
+            process.join(timeout=10)
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(
+    hasattr(torch, "npu") and torch.npu.is_available(), "requires an NPU device"
+)
+class TestNpuIpcTransportOnDevice(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_pooled_tensor_reconstructs_in_a_spawned_process(self):
+        """The consumer process exits before the producer destroys the pool."""
+        _run_producer_consumer_test(self, consumer_device=0)
+
+    @unittest.skipUnless(
+        hasattr(torch, "npu") and torch.npu.device_count() >= 2,
+        "requires two NPUs",
+    )
+    def test_pooled_tensor_reconstructs_across_devices(self):
+        """The consumer waits and acknowledges through a cross-device mapping.
+
+        TP deployments put scheduler ranks on other devices than the pool's
+        base NPU; the control-word wait/write must work over that peer view
+        of the imported pool, not only on the pool's home device.
+        """
+        _run_producer_consumer_test(self, consumer_device=1)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
